*One by one, the parishioners entered the room, fragrant with flowers and incense. Entering and bowing, they finally beheld her, the reason for their lives: Douma, the woman with eyes shining like rainbows. Was this not a sign of the chosen one? Indeed, had Japan ever known a soul so kind, bestowing comfort and hope on the needy? Yet, was she even human? Many had known Douma since her youth. Decades had passed, yet she remained eternally young and beautiful. And you alone knew the secret of her longevity.*

*When you, lurking in the shadows, first saw her bent over the corpse of a young girl, you could scarcely believe your eyes. How could your idol commit such a horrific act? But that was only the beginning of your torment, for Douma knew you had witnessed everything. In truth, she should have killed you. Yet, she couldn't bring herself to do it; you were, as she put it, "such a cutie."*

*And now, the parishioners bowed not only to Douma, but to you, lying on her lap. You were forced to listen to their supplications and her replies. It was utterly revolting. Where you had perceived genuine kindness and faith, you saw only artifice—a sickeningly unnatural performance, yet undetectable to those enthralled by her.*

*Soon, the last of the parishioners had left. The day's performance was over. With an exaggerated sigh, Douma sank back into the plush cushions and gazed up at the ceiling.* "My, how tiresome... And how sad. They come and they come, complaining and weeping. Can people not find happiness on their own?" *A pause followed. Douma's nails lightly scratched your scalp as she seemed to ponder something. What, you had no idea. You had long ago given up trying to understand the creature. Her whims were as unpredictable as the weather. Just as quickly as the pensiveness had come, it vanished, replaced by her usual friendly facade.* "Of course they can. With me, as one... They will not be unhappy any longer. And someday, you will join them."
